author: Meera (DevOps)
method: Anonymous read-only HTTPS GET of public URLs only. crawl.py downloads index.html plus every referenced JS/CSS and follows import() and __vite__mapDeps to closure. Origins are classified by reading the call site around each string in the bundle, not by the string alone.

live_build.baked_api_base: https://influora.in/api/v1 (absolute, not relative: const Th / SL)
live_build.closure_note: The only lazy chunks are the 4 import() targets plus the 6-entry __vite__mapDeps list. The one other import() is react-router's framework-mode route loader (import(e.module)), which SPA mode never calls. The CSS has no url() or @import, so it loads nothing.
live_build.prerender_not_applied: The live index.html is the static crawler fallback from index.html (12,391 bytes), not scripts/prerender.mjs output, so prerender did not run for this deploy.

topology_observed.www_influora_in: Returns 200 with the same index.html (ETag 6ab25b28-3067) and does NOT redirect to the apex. Because the API base is hard-coded to https://influora.in, a visitor on www makes CROSS-ORIGIN API calls, and CORS allows them (preflight returns Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://www.influora.in, credentials true). So connect-src must list https://influora.in explicitly. 'self' alone breaks every API call on www.
topology_observed.api_location_headers: Spring already sends its own security headers on /api/v1/*: HSTS max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains, X-Frame-Options DENY, CSP default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'none', Referrer-Policy no-referrer, X-Content-Type-Options nosniff. If nginx adds headers at server level and location /api/ has none of its own, /api/ inherits them and sends duplicate or conflicting headers. Keep the SPA headers out of /api/, or scope them to the static locations.
topology_observed.ai_influora_in: GET /healthz returns 200 with no security headers. The live SPA never references it (see meera).

origins.evidence: /assets/*.js, /site-tags.js, /favicon + icons, /product-shots/*.png, /stitch-media/*.jpg, /brand/mark.png, /videos/*.mp4 and /placeholder-video*.mp4 (default walkthrough videos; zLe={} so no VITE_WALKTHROUGH_* override is baked in).

const Th="https://influora.in/api/v1" and const SL="https://influora.in/api/v1" are used by fetch() for every API call, including Meera chat, the streamed turns (fetch + body.getReader SSE parsing, no EventSource) and voice speak/transcribe. Must be explicit for the www host. Also https://influora.in/api/v1/webhooks/woocommerce, which is displayed copy, not fetched.

site-tags.js injects <script src=https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtm.js?id=GTM-K7LNG26G>. GTM then loads gtag/js?id=G-CLTL0Y6L44 from the same host. Google's GA4 CSP guidance also lists *.googletagmanager.com for img and connect. The noscript iframe ns.html needs frame-src only for JS-disabled visitors.
gtag-G-CLTL0Y6L44.js builds https://{subdomain.}google-analytics.com/g/s/collect (the GA4 collect endpoint, via sendBeacon/fetch, with an image fallback).
gtag builds https://{subdomain.}analytics.google.com/g/s/collect

Both gtm.js and gtag reference https://www.google.com/ccm/geo and www.google.com (conversion/ads measurement, Google signals). No Ads or Floodlight tag is configured in the container, so these are probably unused. Allowing them is low risk; leaving them out risks only console CSP reports.
gtag: Google signals / demographics beacon. Fires only if Google signals is enabled in GA4 admin, which is not verifiable anonymously.
GTM template __cvt_MQDKZ injectScript('https://www.clarity.ms/tag/yh2rsgpkvq?ref=gtm')
The Clarity tag loader inserts https://scripts.clarity.ms/0.8.70/clarity.js
Clarity tag config upload: https://k.clarity.ms/collect (XHR POST / sendBeacon). The host letter is assigned per project and can change, so use https://*.clarity.ms.
Clarity tag: (new Image).src='https://c.clarity.ms/c.gif' on load.

Loaded 3 ways: (1) GTM template tag __cvt_5RM3Q (pixel 624599723914394) through injectScript; (2) GTM Custom HTML tag_id 3 (see gtm_findings); (3) the bundle's own Tjt() inserts https://connect.facebook.net/en_US/fbevents.js for the Festival Box sponsor pixel. fbevents.js then loads connect.facebook.net/signals/config/<id> and signals/plugins/* from the same host.

fbevents.js sends /tr by new Image() GET, sendBeacon and fetch POST. For large payloads it creates a hidden <form method=post action=ENDPOINT target=<iframe name>> pointing at www.facebook.com/tr, so a form-action 'self' policy silently blocks that fallback. The iframe it creates is about:blank (no frame-src entry needed); the form response lands in it, so frame-src www.facebook.com may be needed. Not verified.
fbevents.js constant SGW_INSTANCE_FRL. Used only when a Conversions API Gateway is configured for the pixel. The signals config for 624599723914394 does not reference it. Omit it.
bundle: const kqe='https://checkout.razorpay.com/v1/checkout.js' injected by Eqe() (id razorpay-checkout-sdk) for wallet top-up and escrow funding. Runs behind login only.
Referenced 7 times in the public checkout.js (the checkout iframe plus API calls). The bundle never references it directly. Inferred from vendor code, not observed at runtime.
checkout.js telemetry (also lumberjack-cx / lumberjack-metrics). Inferred from vendor code only.
checkout.js, 8 refs (logos and images, most inside the api.razorpay.com iframe). Inferred.

qLe() maps walkthrough video URLs to <iframe src=https://www.youtube.com/embed/ID>. It runs only when a VITE_WALKTHROUGH_VIDEO_* env var holds a YouTube URL. The live build bakes zLe={}, so the defaults (/videos/*.mp4) are used and this iframe is DEAD in this build. Needed only if that env var is ever set.
Same resolver and same status as YouTube: dead in this build.
qLe() accepts <video> file URLs on influora.in and *.influora.in (VLe). It is dead in this build for the same reason, so 'self' covers the defaults.

Not a string in the bundle. It arrives as API data. docs/docs/features/uploads-storage.md says deliverable media, proof screenshots and portfolio covers are served as 15-minute presigned R2 GET URLs. The host is <account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com, but the account id lives only in the server .env, which was not read. The R2_PUBLIC_URL default https://r2.influora.com may also apply. See unverified.

Not in the bundle. It arrives as API data: the Content Performance post thumbnails (F-1788, ff94cba) and Meta profile pictures are hotlinked. Per the established brief, not re-observed here (it needs an authenticated analytics view).

schemes_needed.blob:: media-src: Meera voice playback URL.createObjectURL(blob) -> new Audio(url) (two call sites). Also window.open(blob text/html) to print a report. That opens a blob document that inherits this CSP and may need the same script/style allowances. Downloads (a[href=blob:], download attr) need no CSP entry.
schemes_needed.data:: media-src: MeeraDemoPlayer (Remotion) embeds zr='data:audio/mp3;base64,...' (silent autoplay-unlock clip). img-src data: is standard for Radix/SVG and safe to keep. font-src: none needed. The CSS has no @font-face and no url(), so Inter and JetBrains Mono fall back to system fonts.
schemes_needed.mediastream: getUserMedia plus MediaRecorder record voice locally and upload it through fetch to /api. No CSP entry is needed, but a Permissions-Policy must keep microphone=(self) or Meera voice breaks.
schemes_needed.worker: No new Worker / SharedWorker in the bundle. Clarity uses CompressionStream, not a worker. worker-src 'self' is enough (blob: is optional).

style_src_requirement: 'unsafe-inline' is required in style-src. Runtime <style> injection: the react-remove-scroll style singleton (LDe: createElement('style'), honours __webpack_nonce__ only), React 19 hoisted <style precedence> resources, and the Remotion player (MeeraDemoPlayer: head.prepend(style)). Style hashes cannot cover dynamic text. Inline style="" attributes set through the CSSOM (element.style) are not governed by CSP.
script_src_eval: No eval( or new Function( in any first-party chunk. GTM sandboxed templates (__cvt_*) and gtag do not need 'unsafe-eval'. Omit 'unsafe-eval'.

inline_scripts_in_index_html.purpose: JSON-LD Organization schema (type=application/ld+json). It is a data block that is never executed, so script-src does not govern it and it needs no hash. The hash is recorded in case a policy author prefers to list it anyway.

inline_scripts_note: There is no executable inline script in the live index.html. The GTM bootstrap is the external same-origin /site-tags.js, and the module entry is external. There is no theme-flash script. Caveat: if a future deploy runs scripts/prerender.mjs, the prerendered HTML may contain other inline blocks (e.g. per-route JSON-LD from <Seo>). Recompute hashes against THAT artifact, not this one.

inline_style_attributes_in_index_html.note: Parsed only when JS is disabled. Harmless if blocked.

tags.content: inline
tags.csp: WILL BE BLOCKED under any script-src without 'unsafe-inline' or a nonce. GTM injects it as an inline script whose text we do not control. This is the duplicate pixel from the GTM memory note. Recommendation: DELETE tag 3 in the GTM UI, because tag 5 already fires PageView for the same pixel. Do NOT add 'unsafe-inline' to accommodate it. Until it is deleted, expect one CSP violation report per page.

gtm_findings.other_hosts_in_container_runtime: www.google.com, www.googleadservices.com, adservice.google.com, pagead2.googlesyndication.com, ade.googlesyndication.com, ad.doubleclick.net, cct.google, www.youtube.com/m.youtube.com (YouTube video trigger support). These are generic GTM runtime capabilities, and no configured tag uses them. Excluded.

meera.evidence: grep -c 'ai.influora' returns 0 in all 8 chunks. Every Meera call is fetch(`${SL}${Xg(role)}/...`) with SL=https://influora.in/api/v1 and Xg -> '/meera' | '/creator/meera': sessions, messages, credits, brand-profile, voice/speak, voice/transcribe, and /workspaces/me/meera/interactions/option-tapped. Streaming uses fetch plus a ReadableStream reader, not EventSource or WebSocket.
meera.csp_consequence: ai.influora.in does NOT need to be in connect-src for this build. Spring proxies Meera server-side. The repo template's ${CSP_MEERA_ORIGIN} is unnecessary for the live SPA.

dropped_as_not_loaded.reason: Only <link rel=preconnect> in index.html. No stylesheet or @font-face loads from them (the CSS has 0 url() and 0 @font-face; no JS injects a fonts link). A preconnect needs no CSP entry. The warm-up is wasted and can be deleted.

Avatar strings inside MOCK constants (IL bid list, zK conversation list). The live build has die='live' (isApiLive true), and per the mock-constants memory these sit behind if(!isApiLive()) returns. Not proven for every consumer, so listed in unverified. Recommendation: omit them. If one leaks, it shows a broken avatar image, not a security hole.

dropped_as_not_loaded.origin: https://developers.facebook.com, https://gsap.com, https://react.dev, https://reactrouter.com, https://radix-ui.com, https://github.com, http://fb.me, https://www.remotion.dev, https://remotion.dev, https://docs.pmnd.rs, https://jcgt.org, https://tailwindcss.com
dropped_as_not_loaded.reason: Docs links in error messages, licence comments or markdown copy (e.g. Meta Platform Terms in the privacy copy)
<input placeholder> text and <a href> profile links built by gwt(); navigation only
react-router history fallback base and a Remotion dev message
Top-level window.location.href navigation returned by the API. CSP does not govern it.

would_break_if_shipped_as_is: media-src is absent, so it falls back to default-src 'self'. That blocks Meera voice playback (blob:) and the Remotion data:audio clip.
connect-src relies on ${CSP_API_ORIGIN}. It must resolve to https://influora.in or the www host loses the API.
form-action 'self' blocks the Meta Pixel large-payload form POST to www.facebook.com/tr (a silent drop, not a crash)
frame-src has no youtube/vimeo entry. That is dead code today, but it breaks the moment a VITE_WALKTHROUGH_VIDEO_* URL is set.
stale_or_unneeded: ${CSP_MEERA_ORIGIN}: the live bundle never calls ai.influora.in
https://capi-automation.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com in script-src: not in fbevents.js 2.9.406 or in this pixel's signals config
https://tagassistant.google.com in frame-src: needed only for GTM Preview/debug mode (keep it if the team uses preview on prod)
comparison_with_repo_template.img_src_https_wildcard: The template uses img-src 'self' data: blob: https:. That is pragmatic given the API-supplied image hosts (R2 presigned, Instagram CDN, fbcdn). An explicit list is tighter but needs the R2 account host, which cannot be verified from here.

unverified: Razorpay runtime origins (api.razorpay.com frame and XHR, lumberjack*.razorpay.com, cdn.razorpay.com, checkout-static-next.razorpay.com, browser.sentry-cdn.com). Taken from the public checkout.js only. Checkout opens only in authenticated top-up and escrow flows, which cannot be exercised anonymously.

The exact R2 presigned host (<account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com, or r2.influora.com). The account id is only in the server env, which was deliberately not read. Whether downloads are fetched with fetch() (connect-src) or only used as img/video src.
Instagram/Facebook CDN image hosts for Content Performance thumbnails and profile pictures. They need an authenticated analytics view.
Whether Google signals / Ads features are on in GA4 admin (decides whether stats.g.doubleclick.net and www.google.com are actually hit).
Whether the Meta Pixel form-POST fallback also needs frame-src https://www.facebook.com for its response iframe.
Whether the mock avatar constants (i.pravatar.cc, images.unsplash.com) are fully unreachable in live mode. Every consumer was not traced.
Whether the Clarity upload host letter (k.) is stable. Assume it can change and use *.clarity.ms.
The contents of the prerendered HTML if prerender runs in a future deploy (possible extra inline JSON-LD blocks with different hashes).

No browser session was run. The inventory is static analysis of the live bytes plus vendor scripts, not observed network traffic under a report-only CSP. Recommend shipping Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only first.
